---
title: "Code formatting and lint checks"
---

These are contributor tools, not prerequisites for using proj.

Each PR checks existing changed Rust/R source against its Git merge base. Rust
uses rustfmt and Clippy from Rust 1.95.0. R uses
[Air 0.12.0](https://posit-dev.github.io/air/) and
[lintr 3.4.0](https://lintr.r-lib.org/). Air is the formatter used by the official
VS Code Air extension and Positron. CI checksums bind the official tool downloads.
No tools are installed in a user's R library.

The repository rustfmt.toml, air.toml and .lintr files are shared settings:
Rust 2024 style, Air's 80-column/two-space layout and lintr's default checks.
Only touched maintained files are formatted.

## Checks and warning policy

- rustfmt reads selected .rs files through stdin, without traversing or changing
  untouched child modules.
- R source scripts (.R, .r, .Rprofile) use Air, then lintr. Embedded R Markdown/
  Quarto chunks keep their separate renderer/example checks; whole markup files
  are not passed to a plain-R parser.
- Clippy analyzes the workspace and all targets when Rust/Cargo inputs change.
  It is not per-file lint. Compiler failures and new diagnostics anywhere fail.
  Existing warnings with unchanged code, message and normalized expression
  remain visible in a same-toolchain merge-base report, avoiding unrelated cleanup.
  No lint is globally disabled.
- Rename destinations, deleted files, spaces/newlines and no-file cases are
  handled explicitly. Filenames are argument-array values, never shell expansion.

Check mode preserves source bytes and never pushes commits. Artifacts contain a
formatting patch and lint reports. Explicit format mode changes only a disposable
runner checkout; it never commits or pushes. Verify its exact run/head, review
the patch and apply with git apply -p2, then rerun checks.

Fork PRs use pull_request, a read-only token, no persisted checkout credentials,
no custom secrets and no write-back. They never use pull_request_target.
R tools install only in a temporary CI library. The pinned image supplies base
R/dependencies; extra lintr/rex/lazyeval/xmlparsedata sources have fixed checksums.

Use Rust Analyzer/rustfmt and the official
[Air VS Code/Positron extension](https://posit-dev.github.io/air/editor-vscode.html)
for editor formatting. Enable format-on-save in personal editor settings if
desired; this repository does not change those settings.


The pinned diagnostic image uses R 4.6. The first remote setup exposed that
CRAN rex 1.2.1 imports lazyeval 0.2.2, which cannot load against that R C API
(undefined PREXPR symbol). The lint tools therefore use official rex source at
7a8fb36a29919c3d447cc823c672af9b5cf1fd68, checksum-verified, which uses withr
instead. This is an isolated CI tool dependency, not an analysis dependency or
an alteration to a user's R library. Lintr remains pinned to 3.4.0.


Clippy's initial full-stack run found a pre-existing deny-by-default permission
literal lint in an untouched fixture; the equivalent octal spelling is corrected.
For diagnostic comparison only, the old baseline uses --cap-lints warn so that
pre-existing deny-by-default lints can be inventoried. The current head does not
use that cap: errors and new warnings block. Existing warnings remain visible
when their code, message and normalized source expression are unchanged, even
when rustfmt changes whitespace in the containing file. This avoids converting
a feature delivery into a general cleanup of historic build code. Compiler
failures in either checkout remain blocking.


The optional Xet helper is compiled inside the pinned upstream workspace. Its
integration job runs Clippy on that actual binary target too, records diagnostics,
and rejects helper warnings or target compilation failures. The proj workspace
check alone does not cover an injected external-workspace source file. Upstream
warnings outside our helper remain upstream findings, not edits to preserved code.
